text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Federal Communications Minister Richard Alston has told News Ltd executive chairman Ken Cowley not to worry about access to the Minister, following Cowley's accusation last weekend that the Government listens more to the Packer "end of town". In a reportcard of the media moguls, Alston said Kerry Packer approached the Government with a firm but balanced approach, News Ltd's was more selective and Conrad Black was the most aggressive of the players. Page 1.

International Monetary Fund managing director Michel Camdessus has urged the Federal Government to implement major tax reform to facilitate more ambitious fiscal consolidation than so far proposed. The IMF chief also said Australia should aim for a strucural surplus, rather than a balanced Budget and the Reserve Bank could consider tightening its 2-3 per cent inflation target. Page 3.

Woolworths Ltd managing director Reg Clairs said yesterday the group could strike a fast-food and petrol-retailing venture with one of the big four petrol retailers within the next 12 months. Such a venture would complement Woolworths' existing supermarket petrol retailing deal with Burmah Fuels and Mitsui, which is estimated to eventually earn Woolworths additional annual sales of A$750 million. Page 35.

Newcrest Mining's share price rose by 60 cents to a high of A$5.20 yesterday before closing at A$4.92 on the back of speculation that London-based mining group Minorco was looking at a possible takeover bid. Minorco bought Mercury Asset Management's stake in Newcrest at A$5.60 a share. Page 35.

After being elected as the new president of the NRMA yesterday, merchant banker Nick Whitlam pledged to reform the way the motorists' association is run, saying its structure had become too complex and worked against it being run in an effective way. Whilam said the board process needs to be simplified and directors should be more accountable to members. Page 35.

Carlton & United Breweries chief executive Nuno D'Aquino claimed yesterday that CUB's share of the Australian market has increased to 56 per cent, leaving Lion Nathan's share at 40.6 per cent. D'Aquino said CUB's share was rising, while Lion was in "disaray as one executive after another departs, and its market share declines". Page 36.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The investment community is preparing a warm welcome for the A$8 billion partial sale of communications giant Telstra, with analysts predicting the carrier will play a central role in a telecommunications sector on the Australian stock market. Brokers preict there will be little difficulty in the market absorbing the float as they claim many institutions are already earmarking funds to secure a stake in the float. Page 19.

A major communications service provider has been forced to quit the industry just months after mobile phone reseller Digicall went into receivership. The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has announced ACW Services, a service provider with moe than A$100 million annual revenue, will cease trading as of next week. Page 19.

The Federal Government has informally agreed to a parliamentary inquiry into the future of the Australian steel industry. Industry Minister John Moore has indicated that he would like union leaders to contribute to the inquiry and he has even suggested tht ACTU president Jennie George and the Australian Workers Union suggest possible terms of reference. Page 19.

23-year old James Murdoch will join siblings Lachlan and Elisabeth as senior executives of The News Corp Ltd. James, the third Murdoch junior to join the family company, is thought unlikely to challenge Lachlan, 25, as the favourite to succeed father and chairman Rupert Murdoch. James will manage News' 50 per cent owned Mushroom Records label and possibly its wholly owned Festival Records. Page 19.

Phoenix-styled satellite pay-TV operator Australis Media Ltd has scaled back its operating losses with a A$51.1 million net loss for the opening quarter of 1996-97, as its subscriber base continues to weaken. In a statement issued by Australis, the operator claimed it announced the result for the three-month period against a record A$87.7 million deficit for the 1996 June quarter. Page 20.

A surge in Newcrest Mining Ltd's shares was fuelled by rumours of a takeover offer from a number of gold producers of which Normandy Mining was tipped as the lead contender. Newcrest closed the day 32 cents higher at A$4.92. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Stockbrokers and corporate advisers expect the A$8 billion the Federal Government is expected to fetch for the partial sale of communications giant Telstra, is at the lower end of the scale. Some have tipped A$10 billion worth of proceeds for the one-third sale which is expected to hit the market in early 1998. Page 21.

A public slanging match yesterday was a feature of the ongoing beer war between Carlton & United Breweries and Lion Nathan. CUB managing director, Nuno D'Aquino, claimed Australia's biggest brewer had no real competition. Lion responded to the comments by stating it had not resorted to making comments about CUB during the brewer's "darkest days" when it was struggling with crippling debts. Page 21.

Pharmaceutical distributors Australian Pharmaceutical Industries plans to list on the stock exchange next year as part of a bid to launch into Asia and roll out its acquisition strategy in Australia. Pending approval from its 2,400 chemist members, API will pursue listing with an expected market capitalisation of about A$250 million. Page 23.

Australis Media has taken total losses to a staggering A$443 million since it commenced trading less than three years ago, following the satellite pay TV operator's announcement of a net loss of A$51.1 million for the quarter to September. The results also reveal that Australis lost a further 10,000 subscribers during the period with the total falling to 98,000. Page 23.

Competition in the already intense home loan market is set to step up a notch with Societe Generale Australia emerging as a new player in the mortgage securitisation business after launching a A$2 billion residential mortgage-backed commercial paper and note program. Page 23.

Addressing a breakfast in Brisbane, Suncorp/Metway/QIDC chairman John Lamble said the group's interim plan would be to make moves into the southern States, but to concentrate on expanding its Queensland base first. Lamble went on to say that although the group does not see itself as large as the National Australia Bank, it does not perceive that as an impediment to the cost base of the organisation. Page 25.
THE AGE

With the switch by independent senators Brian Harradine and Mal Colston likely to facilitate the passing of the Telstra sale legislation, a partial float of Telstra that values the telecommunications giant at more than A$30 billion could occur at the end of 1997. Australians will be asked for at least A$5.2 billion because only 35 per cent of the shares can be sold to foreigners. Page C1.

Myer's new sports store has 6083 square metres of selling space and offers a basketball court, tennis court and putting green for customers to try out their products. Myer claims it is the biggest sports store in the Southern Hemisphere and the second biggest sports store in the world and will make a decent return on capital, even though it cost close to A$9 million to fit-out. Page C1.

Rupert Murdoch has appointed his youngest son James as vice-president for music and new media of News Corporation. The new chief will make his first public appearance in the job tomorrow at a news conference in Beverly Hills, California, to unveil an Asian music and multimedia joint venture with the Japanese music producer Tetsuya Komuro. Page C1.

Pharmaceutical company Amrad made a strong market debut yesterday, with its shares closing at A$2.20, a 13 per cent premium to its A$1.95 issue price. The Victorian Government has about 17 per cent of Amrad's issued stock and the Commonwealth Bank and GI Insurance are also big shareholders. Page C2.

Pay TV operator Australis Media posted a A$51.1 million loss for the three months to 30 September, compared to a A$87.7 million loss in the previous quarter. Australis increased sales revenue to A$24.6 million and the company's programming supply agreemet with Foxtel contributed A$6.4 million. Page C3.

The Australian Stock Exchange has granted Santos a waiver from the listing rules that require the reporting of drilling and test results from its oil and gas wells, similar to the one granted to BHP Petroleum. The waiver means the listing rules do not aply if the exploration wells are outside Australia or in the zone of cooperation with Indonesia, but they are conditional on the information remaining confidential. Page C3.
